text:
Nikolaj Ehlers doesn't generate many headlines, and that undersells him. He has 15 points in 19 games on 16 minutes a night, mostly as a setup man, and he's the one feeding Jackson Blake on a line with Logan Stankoven.

His goal total is a bit light: 4 goals on 5.3 expected, shooting 9.3% against a usual range nearer 12%. The assists are the real story. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 97th percentile among forwards, with 52% of his shots coming off the rush.

One oddity: Carolina gets 56% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, but the team has been even better without him, so his on-ice numbers trail his teammates'. On a roster this strong, that's not alarming. Evolving-Hockey had him 16th of 401 forwards last season, with real defensive value. Watch the goals: his shooting should come up toward his norm.
headline: Ehlers is the quiet engine on Carolina's top line
